questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Do you have time this afternoon?"
Write the Chinese for "Are there still people upstairs?"
Write the Chinese question meaning "Can you make it back by three o'clock?"
Write the Chinese for "I would like to talk over a matter with you."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ xiǎng hé ni shāngliang yíjiàn shì.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which two words in this unit both mean "free time"?
What is the opposite of lóushang?
Which question form is used in Nǐ … huídelái huíbulái?

answers.answer_text: A choice-type question using the positive and negative potential forms.

articles.text:
Notes on Additional Required Vocabulary

8.  huídelái        to be able to get back in time
9.  kòng(r)         free time, spare time
10. lóushang        upstairs
11. shāngliang      to discuss, to talk over
12. yǒu kòng(r)     to have free time

Here are some sentences illustrating the use of these vocabulary items:

Nǐ sāndiǎn zhōng huídelái        Can you make it back by three o'clock?
huíbulái?
Lóushang hái yǒu rén?            Are there still people upstairs?
Wǒ xiǎng hé ni shāngliang        I would like to talk over a matter
yíjiàn shì.                      with you.
Nǐ jīntian xiàwǔ yǒu kòngr       Do you have time this afternoon?
ma?
